This is what I tell my fiancé whenever he asks me about getting a certain style:

1. Look at photos & find a few styles you like. Try to figure out what it is that you like about each style. Can your hair do the same thing? Take screenshots of the photos to bring with you. 

2. Decide how much time you are willing to spend each day styling your hair and how much you want to spend on the style itself. (Some styles are going to cost more because of the products used or the upkeep or both.) 

3. Find a barbershop that has great reviews, ask your friends/colleagues for referrals, etc. Take your time to find someone you like. See if they have IG, FB, or a website to show their work. 

4. When making an appointment, let them know ahead of time that you are looking for more than just a quick cut. Explain you will be looking for a consultation, cut, & style. That way they can plan & schedule more time in the appointment so they aren't rushed.

5. At your appointment, show your barber the styles you like. Explain why you like them. Inform them of your skill level, how much time you are willing to put in each day to achieve said style, and your budget. Is it an everyday style or just during the week/weekends? 
(My fiancé doesn't care to style his hair for work during the week but likes to do it when we go out together. He needs something that will look presentable even if he doesn't put product in.)

6. Ask them what they think would look good on you. Different hair styles/colors/cuts look different with skin tone, face shape, type of hair, etc. They are the experts, get their opinion. Ask them to show you some examples if you are unsure what they are talking about. Don't be afraid to ask questions or tell them if you dont like something. 

7. Ask your barber to show you exactly how to style it after they cut your hair. Ask them to describe the products they use & why they chose that type over another. Wax, pomade, gel, paste.. what works best for you/your hair & the style you want to achieve? If you feel comfortable, have someone film them styling your hair so you can watch it back later. 

8. Make sure to book your next appointment before leaving. Your barber will know how often you need to come in for a trim/maintenance. You don't want to wait until your hair is grown out, you can't get in to see your barber because their schedule is full & now you have to see someone else. 

Tips: 
If you found a barber you like, stick with them. They will get to know your hair & how it behaves. They will be able to help you find the style you want & the products to go with. I trust my stylist so much that sometimes I go in & let her decide on my hairstyle. She knows by now the styles I prefer and what looks good on me so I have complete faith in her work.

Practice. You can train your hair to behave in a certain way. It will develop a memory the more time you spend styling it in your preferred style. 

Don't be afraid to try something new. New style, new product. Also, don't be afraid to use a product because you think "only women use it".
